name: command-query-responsibility-segregation
context: Separates read and write operations into distinct models, allowing each to be optimized independently. Best for domains with asymmetric read/write patterns where read and write workloads differ significantly in volume, shape, or scaling needs.
benefits: Independent scaling of read/write paths allows each side to match its actual demand profile
Optimized storage technologies: each model can use storage optimized for its workload
Pre-computed projections: read models use denormalized, query-optimized structures
Flexible querying: multiple read models for different query patterns without affecting write side
Reduced contention: eliminates contention between read and write workloads
Clear separation of concerns: commands and queries are fundamentally different operations
Event-driven integration: natural fit with event sourcing and domain events for audit trails
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency: read models updated asynchronously (50-1000ms lag under normal load)
Increased operational complexity: two models to maintain, projection pipelines
Code duplication risk: some logic may need to exist in both models
Event schema evolution burden: old events must remain compatible with new handlers
Projection lag monitoring required: without lag monitoring, stale views go undetected
Storage overhead: maintaining multiple denormalized views increases data storage costs
use_cases: Read-to-write ratio heavily skewed (10:1 or higher)
Multiple query patterns that don't map to write schema
Need to scale reads and writes independently
Different storage technologies needed for reads vs writes
Complex domain with many query patterns requiring optimized views
Audit trail of all changes provides business value
UI needs different data shapes than domain model
Collaborative features where multiple users modify same entities
avoid_when: Simple CRUD operations dominate the domain
Team lacks operational maturity for managing distributed systems
A well-designed CRUD system with caching and read replicas is sufficient
Team cannot yet operate replay and projection recovery tooling
component_types: CommandModel: Handles operations that change state; commands express intent
QueryModel: Handles data retrieval; queries never modify state
CommandBus: Routes commands to their respective handlers
QueryBus: Routes query requests to appropriate query handlers
CommandHandler: Execute business logic for commands, validate rules, persist to write store, emit domain events
QueryHandler: Fetch and transform data from read store into DTOs; no domain logic
EventHandler: Subscribe to domain events and update read models asynchronously
Projection: Subscribe to domain events and update read models asynchronously
ReadStore: Denormalized data optimized for query performance
WriteStore: Normalized data optimized for consistency
anti_patterns: Distributed monolith: using CQRS without proper domain boundaries
Shared database: same database for read and write models defeats purpose
Dual-writing: writing to both models synchronously removes CQRS safety benefits
Missing idempotency: projection handlers must be idempotent
Ignoring projection lag: not monitoring lag leads to stale data
CRUD on read side: rebuilding CRUD logic on read side
Missing freshness budgets: not defining acceptable lag SLOs
Premature event sourcing: adding event sourcing when not needed
design_principles: Command/Query Separation: Commands change state and return nothing (or an ID), Queries read state and return DTOs
Write Model Authoritative: The write side is the only place where business invariants should be enforced
Read Models Derivative: Query stores are downstream materializers with no write authority and no business logic
Eventual Consistency Acceptance: Acknowledge that read models will lag behind write models; define freshness budgets
Idempotent Projections: Events will be delivered multiple times; projection handlers must be idempotent
Separate Optimization: Each model can use storage technology optimized for its specific workload
Explicit Boundary: CQRS is a control boundary between write truth and read convenience
Outbox Pattern: Atomic writes with event publishing to avoid dual-writing pitfalls
best_practices: Start with one bounded context: Prove value in one domain before expanding
Define freshness budgets per read surface: Acceptable lag, pager threshold, replay procedure
Make projections idempotent: Events will be delivered multiple times (at-least-once delivery)
Track SLIs/SLOs separately: Command latency, query latency, projection lag, event delivery
Use outbox pattern: Atomic writes with event publishing
Version command and query payloads: Enable debugging and schema evolution
Keep command side authoritative: Queries never invent state
Automate projection rebuilds: With throttling and snapshot usage
Rollback capability: Feature flags for event schema changes
Observe lag per read surface: Not just at the broker level
Treat projection recovery as first-class runbook: Not an afterthought
Keep team in communication: CQRS patterns require deep understanding across the team
